REFERRAL REASON
Testing for activating variant in BRAF exon 15 in melanoma tissue.

TEST DESCRIPTION
Sanger sequencing of PCR amplified DNA from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue targeting BRAF exon 15, codon 600 and surrounding region. This assay detects common activating variants in the BRAF gene associated with melanoma and response to targeted therapy.

RESULTS
BRAF (NM_004333.6):
- c.1799T>A p.(Val600Glu): NOT DETECTED
- c.1798_1799delGTinsAA p.(Val600Lys): DETECTED at very low level

The BRAF c.1798_1799delGTinsAA p.(Val600Lys) pathogenic variant was detected at very low level in this sample. Neoplastic cell content was estimated at approximately 15% of total nuclei in the specimen analyzed.

SUMMARY
The detected BRAF c.1798_1799delGTinsAA p.(Val600Lys) pathogenic variant affects the same codon as the common c.1799T>A p.(Val600Glu) activating variant. This variant results in substitution of valine with lysine at codon 600 and leads to constitutive activation of the BRAF kinase. BRAF p.Val600Lys variants are found in approximately 5-6% of BRAF-mutated melanomas and are associated with response to BRAF inhibitor therapy (Chapman et al., N Engl J Med 2011;364:2507-16; Long et al., Lancet Oncol 2014;15:323-32).

The low variant allele frequency observed may be due to low neoplastic cell content in the specimen or tumor heterogeneity. Clinical correlation is recommended.

Test performed by: [redacted name], PhD
Reviewed by: [redacted name], MD, PhD
